name: elbow nerve problems overview
title: Tingling, numbness or weakness around the elbow: true sensory loss means a nerve; ulnar neuropathy at the elbow is worked up with Tinel sign, an ulnar sensory map, hand muscle strength and EMG/NCS, and managed with education, avoiding pressure and hyperflexion, then surgery; pronator syndrome compresses the median nerve at pronator teres

root.title: Tingling, numbness or weakness around the elbow: is it a NERVE, and which one?
lines: tingling can come from nerve, muscle, tendon, ligament or joint, or be REFERRED (cardiac?)
TRUE sensory LOSS is neurogenic: map it to one nerve's territory

groups.title: MEDIAN nerve, in the forearm
lines: front of the forearm · lateral 3½ fingers

head: h
Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow
cubital tunnel syndrome
behind the medial epicondyle
pres: • numbness + tingling: medial forearm into ring + little finger
• direct trauma ('funny bone') · leaning on a desk
• elbow bent in sleep · nerve slips on flexion
inv: tap the nerve → tingling down its territory
NOT the medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm, NOT C8
± weak: small hand muscles most affected
tx: neuritis AND mild neuropathy are fully reversible
• towel splint or elbow pad at night
act earlier → ulnar neurolysis or transposition surgery · drugs add little

head: h
Pronator syndrome
median nerve between the 2 heads of pronator teres
pres: Pain + tenderness: top of the front of the forearm
• ↑ sensation: palm side of lateral 3½ fingers + adjacent palm
inv: • carpal tunnel: see WRIST AND HAND PART 2

panels.title: No true sensory loss?
items: think tendon (see the ELBOW TENDINOPATHY chart), joint, ligament or bursa (see the ELBOW chart), or referred pain

panels.title: Ulnar nerve at the WRIST instead?
items: Guyon's canal ('handlebar neuropathy'), less common than at the elbow: see WRIST AND HAND PART 2
